title: Per-route Breakdown Transformer for Granular Cost & Latency Attributions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a durable, auditable transformation layer that consumes raw telemetry (request spans, runtime timing, model selection events, token counts, cache hits) and emits per-route / per-model / per-customer cost+latency line items suitable for the Console and downstream billing systems. This task focuses on the computation and normalization stage: apportion token/runtime cost across cached prefixes, model fallback chains, multi-tenant GPU sharing, and queueing delays so product and finance can present consistent, explainable breakdowns.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Transformation produces per-request line items with fields: route_id, model_id, customer_id, tokens_charged, token_cost_usd, runtime_ms, queue_ms, io_ms, cache_hit_fraction, attribution_method
2) End-to-end reconcile tests: sample of transformed output matches billing ledger within 0.5% on daily aggregates for top 10 customers
3) Latency breakdowns are available in Console for any route, able to slice by model and time window (1h, 24h)
4) Feature-flagged rollout with fallback to existing aggregator; automatic rollback on reconciliation deviation > 1%
5) Unit and integration tests for apportioning logic with edge cases: all-cached prefixes, 0 tokens (instrumentation gaps), multi-model fallbacks
tech_approach: Input: events from kafka topics telemetry.requests (per-request spans) and telemetry.runtime_metrics (per-inference kernel timings)
Transform: a streaming Beam job (Dataflow) that enriches spans with model catalog metadata and applies apportionment rules; see apportionment rules below

Apportionment rules: token-level charge = base_token_cost * (effective_noncache_tokens / total_effective_tokens); allocate prefix cache savings proportionally across coalesced requests that share cache keys using causally-linked request IDs

Latency attribution: decompose elapsed into queue_ms (ingest timestamp delta), runtime_ms (sum of kernel durations), io_ms (network + storage), and waiting_ms (contended runtimes). Use sampled detailed traces to calibrate mapping factors
Cost modeling: incorporate runtime GPU-minute rate per model variant and amortize across batched requests using dynamic batch-size-aware allocator
Outputs: normalized Parquet hourly partitions written to analytics S3 and a compact daily rollup pushed to billing DB (Postgres) via upsert API
Observability: add counters for transformed events, reconciliation diff metric, and a dashboard in Grafana; alert if transform lag > 5m or reconciliation drift > 1%
design_decisions: Chosen Beam/Dataflow for fault-tolerant streaming enrichment and windowing semantics; alternative (Spark streaming) rejected due to cold-start latency for per-route metrics
Charge apportionment will be deterministic and idempotent using request lineage IDs to avoid double-charging across retries
Model catalog enrichment performed via a cached side-input with TTL 5m to keep join latency low
Detailed token-level attributions stored only for sampled requests (1%) to control storage costs; aggregates computed for all requests
Security: PII-free outputs; customer_id is internal opaque id, and payloads are encrypted at-rest and in-flight
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: instrumentation gaps (missing spans) can cause under/over-allocation. Mitigation: fallback to conservative allocation heuristic and flag records for manual review
Risk: reconciliation drift with billing legacy pipeline. Mitigation: run in parallel (shadow mode) for 2 weeks, compare diffs, and iterate rules
Risk: increased processing costs for per-request enrichments. Mitigation: aggressive sampling of trace-level data and use of lightweight enrichers for majority of traffic
Risk: latency in transform causing Console staleness. Mitigation: prioritize near-real-time hourly partitions and a low-latency stream for top-100 routes

rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow): 14 days shadowing legacy aggregator for all traffic; do not write to billing DB
Phase 1 (canary): enable writes for top-50 routes (feature flag) for 48h, monitor reconciliation and customer support channels
Phase 2 (ramped): expand to top-500 routes over 1 week if diffs stable
Phase 3 (ga): full enablement with daily reconciliation guardrails and 7-day rollback window
testing_plan: Unit tests: apportionment rules, deterministic idempotency, side-input expiry
Integration tests: end-to-end run with synthetic traces including cached-prefix scenarios
Load tests: simulate peak qps with batching to validate memory usage and Dataflow autoscaling
Reconciliation tests: compare outputs against legacy pipeline for 30-day window and assert thresholds
notes: Keep detailed per-request attributions off by default in Console due to cost; expose aggregated views and an opt-in sampling explorer
Work with Finance to decide rounding rules for per-customer invoices to avoid penny-level ambiguity
